 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Yogesh Khanna

Petitioners file this petition for quashing of the FIR No.658/2015 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Moti Nagar, Delhi against them and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. The marriage between the petitioner No.1 and complainant/ respondent No.2 was solemnized on 05.12.2012 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh.
No child was born from this wedlock.
However, due to matrimonial discord, the couple was living separately from each other and on the complaint of respondent No.2 aforesaid FIR was registered against the petitioners.

During the pendency of proceedings, the couple settled the differences per settlement agreement dated 15.06.2021 and respondent No.2 joined her matrimonial home with petitioner No.1 at Kanpur started living happily.
The police filed the charge sheet against the petitioners.
Pursuant to joining the matrimonial home by respondent No.2, she does not wish to pursue her complaint against any of the petitioners.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 10:29:57 3.

The complainant/respondent No.2 has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, states the matter has been settled with the petitioners having left with no claim against them and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

The learned APP for the State has also no objection, if this petition is Mohendra Kumar & Ors vs State & Anr on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178809988/
1 allowed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The affidavits of parties are on record.

4. Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as complainant has settled all the disputes and joined her matrimonial home with petitioner No.1.
In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioners as it would never entail in conviction of petitioners.

The continuity of proceedings rather hamper the matrimonial life of respondent No.2.
5.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, FIR No.658/2015 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Moti Nagar, Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
MAY 17, 2023 M
